lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! Time for a refresher on Slurm node states.
Why does sinfo show idle star? And why does a node stay down after it came back?
A node with no jobs is idle. When jobs use some of its CPUs, it's mixed, and with all of them, allocated.
slurmctld pings every slurmd. A node that misses a ping gets a star: idle star means idle, but not responding.
If it stays silent for the slurmd timeout, slurmctld marks it down, which kills its jobs and keeps new ones away.
When slurmd registers again, the return to service setting decides. sind sets it so the node comes straight back.
With the Slurm default, an admin has to resume it with scontrol.
Draining is the planned way out. Running jobs finish, but no new ones start.
While jobs still run, it's draining. Once they're done, it's drained, until an admin resumes it.
So: a star means not responding, down means out of service, and drained means taken out on purpose.
Next up: episode seven, Failure drills. See you there!
